questions.stem: The presence of membrane-bounded nucleus is the characteristics of
explanation_steps: Eukaryotic cells (plants, animals, fungi, protists) have a true nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane; prokaryotic cells (bacteria) have only a nucleoid region without a membrane (G9 p.17).
Viruses are not cells at all. Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a prokaryote?
explanation_steps: Cyanobacteria (blue-green bacteria) are prokaryotes – kingdom Monera. The others are eukaryotes. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following properties of life describes maturity?
explanation_steps: Textbook (G9 p.2): 'Development is an orderly sequence of change in shape and function over the lifespan of an organism. Every living organism has a definite period of life, such as birth, growth, maturity, senility and death.'
Maturity is a stage of development. Answer: D.

similar_questions.stem: The sum of all the chemical reactions that take place in an organism is called
explanation_steps: Metabolism = anabolism + catabolism, all the chemical reactions in the body. Answer: B.

questions.stem: If a cell is in isotonic environment, then

options.A: the cell will gain water and burst.
options.B: no water will move across the membrane.
options.C: the cell will lose water and shrink.
options.D: water moves but, there is no net gain or loss of cell volume.

explanation_steps: In an isotonic solution the solute (water) concentration is the same inside and outside the cell (G9 pp.21–22).

Water molecules still cross the membrane in both directions, but at equal rates, so there is no net movement and the cell volume stays the same. Answer: D. (B is the common trap: movement does not stop.)
tips: Hypotonic outside → cell gains water; hypertonic outside → cell loses water (plasmolysis in plants).

similar_questions.stem: A red blood cell placed in distilled water will
explanation_steps: Distilled water is hypotonic to the cell, so water enters by osmosis until the cell bursts (haemolysis). Answer: C.

questions.stem: The most abundant organic compounds used as sources of energy by living organisms are
explanation_steps: Carbohydrates (sugars and starch) are the main and most abundant energy source for living organisms; glucose is the usual respiratory fuel (G9 p.118; G10 p.2).
Lipids store more energy per gram but are used mainly as reserves; proteins are used for growth and repair. Answer: C.

similar_questions.stem: Which nutrient gives the most energy per gram?
explanation_steps: Fats release about 38 kJ/g, compared with about 17 kJ/g for carbohydrates and proteins. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The thick walled chambers of the heart that are responsible for blood pumping are the
explanation_steps: The ventricles have thick muscular walls because they pump blood out of the heart (the left ventricle, pumping to the whole body, is thickest); the atria are thin-walled receiving chambers (G10 pp.49–53).
Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: Which chamber of the heart receives deoxygenated blood from the body?
explanation_steps: The venae cavae bring deoxygenated blood to the right atrium. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The arteries supplying blood to the tissues of the heart are the
explanation_steps: The heart muscle receives its own blood supply through the coronary arteries, which branch from the aorta (G10 pp.52–57).
Renal → kidneys; hepatic → liver; pulmonary arteries carry blood to the lungs; venae cavae are veins. Answer: B.
tips: Blockage of a coronary artery causes a heart attack.

similar_questions.stem: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
explanation_steps: The pulmonary veins are the only veins carrying oxygenated blood. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The two types of immunity in humans are
explanation_steps: Immunity is divided into innate (natural, non-specific, present from birth) and acquired (specific, developed after exposure to antigens, active or passive) (G10 pp.101–104).
Answer: D.

similar_questions.stem: Immunity developed after recovering from measles is
explanation_steps: The body made its own antibodies after a natural infection. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The response of some organisms to variation of oxygen concentration is
explanation_steps: Textbook (G10 p.184): 'Aerotaxis is the response to a variation in oxygen concentration.'
Chemotaxis – chemicals; phototaxis – light; osmotaxis – osmotic concentration; thermotaxis – temperature. Answer: E.

similar_questions.stem: Euglena swimming towards light is an example of
explanation_steps: Movement of a whole organism towards light = positive phototaxis. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The cell theory states that

options.A: cells are the smallest living things.
options.C: there is only one basic type of a cell.
options.D: all living things are made up of cells.
options.E: eukaryotic cells have evolved from prokaryotic cells.

explanation_steps: The cell theory (G9 p.11): all living things are made up of one or more cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; all cells come from pre-existing cells.
Answer: D.

similar_questions.stem: Which scientist concluded that all cells come from pre-existing cells?
explanation_steps: Virchow (1855): 'omnis cellula e cellula'. Answer: B.

questions.stem: For natural selection to contribute to evolution

options.A: variations must exist in a population.
options.B: organisms should develop strong adaptive mechanism.
options.D: variations must be inherited from one generation to the next.

explanation_steps: Natural selection can only change a population over generations if individuals differ (variation) AND the differences are heritable, so that the favoured traits are passed on (neo-Darwinism: 'inheritance of variations resulting from changes in DNA', G12 p.65).

D is the essential condition (heritable variation implies that variation exists). A is also true; C (overproduction) is one of Darwin's observations; B sounds Lamarckian (organisms do not 'develop' adaptations on purpose).
D is keyed; A and E are also accepted because A is true and the examiner may have intended 'All of the above'.
tips: Evolution by natural selection needs: variation + inheritance + differential survival/reproduction.

similar_questions.stem: According to Darwin, which individuals in a population are most likely to survive and reproduce?

options.C: Those best adapted to their environment
options.D: Those that try hardest to change

explanation_steps: 'Survival of the fittest' – the best-adapted individuals leave more offspring. Answer: C.

questions.review_flag: A and D are both true (and C is one of Darwin's postulates), so the item has no single best answer; the examiner may have intended E. D keyed, A and E accepted; teacher to decide.

questions.stem: An inorganic component of bones is
explanation_steps: Textbook (G11 p.56): the inorganic components, about 2/3 of bone, 'consist of mineral salts, largely calcium phosphate', which make bones hard.
Nerves, cartilage and connective tissue are living (organic) tissues. Answer: D.

similar_questions.stem: Which protein gives bone its flexibility and tensile strength?
explanation_steps: Collagen fibres form the organic part of bone. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Lower appendages include the
explanation_steps: The lower limb (leg) contains the femur, patella, tibia, fibula, tarsals, metatarsals and phalanges (G11 pp.58–66).
Radius, ulna, carpus (wrist) and humerus are bones of the upper limb. Answer: A.

similar_questions.stem: The bone of the upper arm is the
explanation_steps: The humerus runs from the shoulder to the elbow. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Where is the antidiuretic hormone (ADH) produced?
explanation_steps: ADH (vasopressin) is released into the blood from the posterior lobe of the pituitary gland and acts on the kidney tubules (G11 pp.3–4).

Strictly, the textbook adds that the posterior pituitary 'does not produce hormones, but it does store and release' ADH and oxytocin – they are made in the hypothalamus. The hypothalamus is not an option, so the pituitary is the best choice. Answer: A.
tips: Made in the hypothalamus → stored/released by the posterior pituitary → acts on the kidney.

similar_questions.stem: Oxytocin is released from the
explanation_steps: Like ADH, oxytocin is stored in and released from the posterior pituitary. Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: ADH is produced in the hypothalamus and only stored/released by the posterior pituitary (the textbook says so). Hypothalamus is not an option; A keyed as the best available answer.

questions.stem: In an ecological hierarchy, one of the following is non-living.
explanation_steps: In the hierarchy of organisation (atom → molecule → cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism → population → community → ecosystem → biosphere), life begins at the level of the cell.
A molecule is a non-living chemical level. Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: A group of organisms of the same species living in the same area at the same time is a
explanation_steps: Same species + same place = population; different species together = community. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which statement is incorrect about lactic acid fermentation?

options.A: It is a type of anaerobic respiration.
options.B: It uses glucose as a source of energy.
options.C: It releases carbon dioxide during the process.
options.D: It doesn’t need oxygen for the release of energy.
options.E: It can be used to make cheese.

explanation_steps: Lactic acid fermentation: glucose → 2 lactic acid + a little energy (2 ATP), without oxygen (G10 p.119). No CO₂ is produced.
Alcoholic fermentation (yeast) is the type that releases CO₂. Lactic acid bacteria are used for yoghurt and cheese. Answer: C.
tips: Lactic: glucose → lactic acid (no CO₂). Alcoholic: glucose → ethanol + CO₂.

similar_questions.stem: During strenuous exercise, the muscle cramps are due to the build-up of
explanation_steps: Muscles respire anaerobically when short of O₂, producing lactic acid. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The branch of biology that deals with the general form of an organism is
explanation_steps: Textbook table of branches (G9 p.3): morphology is the study of the form and structure of organisms.
Physiology – functions; cytology – cells; genetics – heredity; taxonomy – classification. Answer: A.

similar_questions.stem: The study of how body parts function is
explanation_steps: Physiology deals with functions of organisms and their parts. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The pyramid that can never be inverted in an ecological trophic level is the
explanation_steps: Energy is lost (as heat, respiration) at every trophic level, so each level always has less energy than the one below it; the pyramid of energy is always upright (G12 p.113).
Pyramids of numbers (e.g. one tree with many insects) and of biomass (e.g. in water) can be inverted. Answer: C.
tips: Only about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level.

similar_questions.stem: If producers fix 10 000 kJ of energy, about how much reaches the secondary consumers (10% rule)?
explanation_steps: Primary consumers get 10% of 10 000 = 1000 kJ; secondary consumers get 10% of 1000 = 100 kJ.

questions.stem: Muscles that are not stimulated by nerve impulses are
explanation_steps: Textbook (G11 pp.78–79): cardiac muscle 'can continue to function without being stimulated by nerve impulses. Their contractions are also not initiated by the nervous system, but generated within the muscle tissue itself' (auto-rhythmic, pacemaker). Nerves only change the rate.
Skeletal (voluntary) muscles contract only when stimulated by motor nerves; smooth muscle is controlled by autonomic nerves. Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: The natural pacemaker of the heart is the
explanation_steps: The SA node in the right atrium starts each heartbeat. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which organism causes the disease called “African sleeping sickness”?
explanation_steps: African sleeping sickness is caused by the flagellate protozoan Trypanosoma (a mastigophoran), spread by the tsetse fly (G9 pp.69–70).
Plasmodium causes malaria; Entamoeba causes amoebic dysentery; Paramecium is free-living. Answer: A.

similar_questions.stem: Malaria is caused by
explanation_steps: Plasmodium, transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Bacteria that are capable of manufacturing their own food are called
explanation_steps: Autotrophs make their own organic food, by photosynthesis (e.g. cyanobacteria) or chemosynthesis (G9 p.61: Monera include 'chemosynthetic or photosynthetic autotrophs').
Heterotrophic, saprophytic, parasitic bacteria and decomposers all obtain ready-made food. Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: Bacteria that feed on dead organic matter are called
explanation_steps: Saprophytes feed on dead and decaying matter. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Bacterial structures that are short, fine, hair like appendages that may serve as means of attachment to solid surfaces are referred to as
explanation_steps: Pili (fimbriae) are short hair-like appendages used for attachment to surfaces (and for conjugation) (G9 pp.29–30).
Flagella are long whip-like structures for movement; the capsule is a slimy outer layer; plasmids are small DNA rings. Answer: D.

similar_questions.stem: The long whip-like structure used by some bacteria for locomotion is the
explanation_steps: Flagella rotate to push the bacterium along. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which one of the following parasitic organisms is a fungus?
explanation_steps: Candida albicans is a yeast (fungus) that causes candidiasis (thrush); the textbook notes that a number of fungi are pathogenic (G9 p.81).
Entamoeba and Plasmodium are protozoa; Neisseria and E. coli are bacteria. Answer: E.

similar_questions.stem: The fungus from which penicillin was first obtained is
explanation_steps: The textbook (G9 p.81): 'The antibiotic penicillin is produced from a fungus called Penicillium notatum.' Answer: B.

questions.stem: Sponges are members of the phylum
explanation_steps: Sponges are poriferans ('pore-bearers'): their bodies are full of pores through which water is drawn (G9 p.89).
Cnidaria – Hydra and jellyfish; Platyhelminthes – flatworms; Nematoda – roundworms; Mollusca – snails. Answer: A.

similar_questions.stem: Hydra and jellyfish belong to the phylum
explanation_steps: They are cnidarians with stinging cells (cnidocytes). Answer: B.

questions.stem: A nocturnal behavior of some animals is an adaptation to
explanation_steps: The textbook lists nocturnal behaviour among the adaptations of animals of hot, dry regions (G9 p.151): they hide in burrows by day and become active and feed at night, when it is cool, to avoid heat and water loss.
Answer: A.

similar_questions.stem: Thick fur and a thick layer of fat under the skin are adaptations of animals to
explanation_steps: They insulate the body and reduce heat loss in cold climates. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The correct dental formula of an adult human being is
explanation_steps: In each half of each jaw an adult has 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars and 3 molars: i 2/2, c 1/1, pm 2/2, m 3/3 (G10 p.30).
Check: (2 + 1 + 2 + 3) × 2 × 2 = 32 teeth. Answer: B.
tips: The dental formula covers one side only – multiply by 2 for the total.

similar_questions.stem: The dog's dental formula is i 3/3, c 1/1, pm 4/4, m 2/3. How many teeth does an adult dog have?
explanation_steps: Upper jaw, one side: 3 + 1 + 4 + 2 = 10; lower jaw, one side: 3 + 1 + 4 + 3 = 11.
Total = (10 + 11) × 2 sides = 42 teeth.

textbook_ref.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The synthesis of a lipid molecule requires

options.A: three molecules of fatty acid and one molecule of glycerol.
options.B: one molecule of fatty acid and two molecules of glycerol.
options.C: three molecules of fatty acid and two molecules of glycerol.
options.D: three molecules of fatty acid and three molecules of glycerol.
options.E: one molecule of fatty acid and one molecule of glycerol.

explanation_steps: A fat (triglyceride) forms by condensation of one glycerol with three fatty acids, releasing three water molecules (G9 p.121; G10 p.10).
Answer: A.

similar_questions.stem: How many water molecules are released when one triglyceride is formed?
explanation_steps: One ester bond (and one H₂O) forms for each of the three fatty acids. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which group of carbohydrates is insoluble in water?
explanation_steps: Monosaccharides (glucose, fructose) and disaccharides (sucrose, lactose) are sweet and soluble; polysaccharides (starch, cellulose, glycogen) are large polymers, not sweet and insoluble in water (G9 pp.118–120; G10 pp.3–5).
Answer: C.

similar_questions.stem: Which carbohydrate is the storage form of glucose in animals?
explanation_steps: Animals store glucose as glycogen in the liver and muscles. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Obesity is a condition of overweight caused due to excess
explanation_steps: Obesity is the storage of excess body fat. The textbook discusses it with lipids (G10 p.11): diets rich in fat, and taking in more kilojoules than are used, make people overweight; 'being very fat is called obesity'.
A is keyed. Excess carbohydrate intake is also converted to fat, so B is also accepted.

similar_questions.stem: A person takes in 12 000 kJ a day but uses only 10 000 kJ. What is likely to happen over time?
explanation_steps: The surplus 2000 kJ a day is stored mainly as fat. Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: Obesity is excess body fat caused by excess energy intake from fats and/or carbohydrates; A keyed (textbook context), B also accepted.

questions.stem: All of the following food types are sources of carbohydrates, except
explanation_steps: Textbook (G10 p.3): 'Carbohydrates are obtained from sugar cane, milk, bread, potatoes, wheat, pasta, cereals, injera and rice.'
Butter is almost pure fat (a lipid source). Answer: C.

similar_questions.stem: Which food is the best source of protein?
explanation_steps: Legumes such as beans, lentils and peas are rich in protein. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The human disease, goiter, is associated with the deficiency of
explanation_steps: The textbook mineral table (G10 p.13): iodine (sea salt, iodised table salt, seafood) regulates the rate of body processes (via thyroxine); deficiency → goitre (swelling of the thyroid).
Iron deficiency → anaemia; calcium → rickets/weak bones. Answer: D.

similar_questions.stem: Deficiency of calcium and vitamin D in children causes
explanation_steps: Soft, bent bones (rickets). Answer: B.

questions.stem: Water is the most important nutrient of all living cells, because it is
explanation_steps: Water is the universal solvent, cools the body (sweat evaporation), and is the medium of transport in blood, lymph and sap (G10 pp.19–20).
Water provides no energy (no kilojoules). So A, B and C apply but not D. Answer: E.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following nutrients provides energy?
explanation_steps: Of these only carbohydrates are oxidised to release energy. Answer: D.

questions.stem: The genotype of a person who is homozygous for blood group B is
explanation_steps: Homozygous = two identical alleles. Blood group B can be IᴮIᴮ (homozygous) or Iᴮi (heterozygous) (G12 pp.40–41).
IⁱIⁱ is group O; IᴮIᴬ is AB; IᴮIⁱ is heterozygous B. Answer: D.

similar_questions.stem: A person with genotype Iᴬi has blood group
explanation_steps: Iᴬ is dominant over i, so the phenotype is group A (heterozygous). Answer: A.

questions.review_flag: Option B writes the O allele as Iᴼ instead of i (non-standard notation); answer unaffected.

questions.stem: The human digestive system is a long muscular, tube like structure approximately ____ in length if stretched out.
explanation_steps: Textbook (G10 p.23): 'The digestive system is a long, muscular, tube-like structure, approximately eight metres in length.'
Answer: C.

similar_questions.stem: The longest part of the human alimentary canal is the
explanation_steps: The small intestine is about 6 m long. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The mammalian teeth that are used for seizing prey and tearing flesh are called
explanation_steps: Canines are pointed teeth for seizing, piercing and tearing; incisors cut/bite; premolars and molars grind (G10 pp.29–30).
Answer: C.

similar_questions.stem: The chisel-shaped front teeth used for biting and cutting are
explanation_steps: Incisors have sharp flat edges for cutting. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct about the lymph nodes? They

options.B: are involved in removing bacteria and other materials.
options.C: produce some types of white blood cells.

explanation_steps: Textbook (G10 p.90): 'Lymph nodes filter the lymph, removing bacteria and other materials. Some types of white blood cells (phagocytes and lymphocytes) are produced in the lymph nodes.' So A, B and C are all correct.
D is not a function of lymph nodes (digested fats are absorbed by the lacteals of the villi and carried by lymph vessels). Strictly, E is therefore false, but it is the examiner's likely intention.
E keyed; A, B and C are also accepted.

similar_questions.stem: Which organ is the largest lymphatic organ and destroys old red blood cells?
explanation_steps: The spleen filters blood and removes worn-out red cells. Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: A, B and C are all textbook statements and D (absorb digested food) is false, so 'All of the above' is strictly wrong and there is no single best answer. E keyed as the likely intention; A, B, C also accepted. Teacher to decide.

questions.stem: The branch of chemistry that studies the detection, monitoring, transport and chemical transformation of substances in air, water and soil is
explanation_steps: Environmental chemistry studies the sources, reactions, transport and effects of chemical substances in air, water and soil (G9 p.4).
Organic – carbon compounds; industrial – large-scale production; nuclear – changes in nuclei; biochemistry – chemistry of living things. Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: The branch of chemistry that deals with the chemical processes in living organisms is
explanation_steps: Biochemistry is the chemistry of life processes. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following substances is an element?
explanation_steps: An element contains only one kind of atom (G9 pp.20–22). Oxygen (O₂) is an element.
Hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), water (H₂O) and table salt (NaCl) are compounds; air is a mixture. Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a compound?
explanation_steps: CO₂ is two elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio. Brass and air are mixtures; N₂ and Fe are elements. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about trends in the periodic table?

options.B: Atomic radius decreases down a group.
options.C: Ionization energy increases across a period.
options.D: Atomic radius increases across a period.
options.E: Ionization energy decreases across a period.

explanation_steps: Across a period the nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same shell, so atoms get smaller and hold their electrons more tightly: ionization energy and electronegativity increase, atomic radius decreases (G10 pp.24–31).
Down a group new shells are added: radius increases, ionization energy and electronegativity decrease. Only C is true. Answer: C.

similar_questions.stem: Which element has the largest atomic radius?
explanation_steps: Radius increases down group IA (Li < Na < K) and decreases across a period. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The chemical formula of laughing gas is
explanation_steps: Laughing gas is dinitrogen monoxide (nitrous oxide), N₂O, used as a mild anaesthetic; the textbook names N₂O 'dinitrogen monoxide' in its table of binary molecular compounds (G9 p.96).
NO = nitrogen monoxide, NO₂ = nitrogen dioxide, N₂O₃ and N₂O₅ are dinitrogen tri- and pentoxide. Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: What is the name of N₂O₅?
explanation_steps: Prefixes: di- (2 N), penta- (5 O) → dinitrogen pentoxide. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements has the highest non-metallic character?
explanation_steps: Non-metallic character = tendency to gain electrons; it increases across a period and up a group, following electronegativity (G10 p.32).
Na, Ca and Fe are metals. Of the non-metals, Br (group VIIA, electronegativity 2.8) is more non-metallic than C (group IVA, 2.5). Answer: E.

similar_questions.stem: Which element is the most metallic?
explanation_steps: Metallic character decreases across period 3 from Na to Cl. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Anything that has mass and occupies space is
explanation_steps: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space (volume) (G9 p.6).
Light and sound are forms of energy, not matter. Answer: C.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT matter?
explanation_steps: Heat is a form of energy – it has no mass and takes up no space. Answer: C.

questions.stem: In a neutral atom, the number of

options.A: protons is greater than the number of electrons.
options.B: protons is equal to the number of electrons.
options.C: electrons is less than the number of protons.
options.D: protons is greater than the number of neutrons.
options.E: protons is always less than the number of neutrons.

explanation_steps: An atom is electrically neutral because it has as many electrons (−) as protons (+) (G9 p.50).
The number of neutrons can be less, equal or greater (e.g. H-1 has none). Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: An atom has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. How many electrons does the neutral atom have?
explanation_steps: Neutral atom: electrons = protons = 11.

questions.stem: Which of the following represents an intensive property?
explanation_steps: Intensive properties do not depend on the amount of substance (melting point, boiling point, density, colour); extensive properties do (mass, volume, length, heat capacity) (G9 p.14).

questions.stem: An object that can be seen by a magnifying glass, has to be located at a distance

options.A: smaller than the focal length of the converging lens.
options.B: smaller than the focal length of the concave lens.
options.C: equal to the focal length of the lens.
options.E: greater than the focal length of the concave lens.

explanation_steps: A magnifying glass (simple microscope) is a converging (convex) lens with the object placed between the lens and its focal point; it then forms a virtual, upright, magnified image (G11 pp.23–27, 35–36).
A concave lens always gives diminished images. Answer: A.

similar_questions.stem: Where must an object be placed in front of a convex lens to obtain a real image of the same size?
explanation_steps: At 2F the image is at 2F on the other side: real, inverted, same size. Answer: C.

questions.stem: When we look at objects closer to our eyes,

options.A: the ciliary muscles of our eyes expand.
options.B: the curvature of our eye lenses decrease.
options.C: our eye lenses become thicker and their focal length increase.
options.D: the curvature of our eye lenses increase.
options.E: our eye lenses become thinner and their focal length decrease.

explanation_steps: Accommodation (G11 pp.44–47): for near objects the ciliary muscles contract, the suspensory ligaments slacken, and the lens becomes thicker (more curved), so its focal length decreases and the near image still falls on the retina.
Only D is fully correct (C has the wrong focal-length change; E has the wrong thickness). Answer: D.

questions.stem: The elements that can produce extremely strong permanent magnets are
explanation_steps: The strongest permanent magnets are rare-earth magnets – neodymium (Nd₂Fe₁₄B) and samarium–cobalt alloys.
Iron, cobalt and nickel are ferromagnetic and are used in ordinary magnets (e.g. Alnico), but rare-earth magnets are far stronger; magnetite is a natural magnetic ore, not an element. Answer: C.

similar_questions.stem: Which material is best for making a permanent magnet?
explanation_steps: Steel keeps its magnetism (high retentivity); soft iron loses it easily and is used for electromagnets. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Electromagnetic waves travel

options.A: faster in gases than in solids and liquids.
options.B: faster in solids than in liquids and gases.
options.C: faster in liquids than in gases and solids.
options.D: at the same speed in all solids.
options.E: at the same speed in all liquids.

explanation_steps: The speed of light in a medium is v = c/n. Gases have n ≈ 1.0003, liquids ≈ 1.3, solids ≈ 1.5 (glass) to 2.4 (diamond), so EM waves are fastest in gases (and fastest of all in vacuum) (G11 pp.7–10, 213).
Different solids/liquids have different n, so D and E are false. (Sound behaves the opposite way.) Answer: A.
tips: Light: fastest in vacuum/gases. Sound: fastest in solids.

questions.stem: In the phenomenon of photo electric effect,

options.A: the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons depends linearly on the intensity of the incident radiation.
options.B: the intensity of the incident radiation is proportional to the number of photons per unit area per unit time.
options.C: photo electric current is independent on the intensity of the incident radiation.
options.D: the intensity of the incident radiation is independent of the frequency of the radiation.
options.E: electrons are emitted from the surface of the metal provided that the frequency of the incident radiation is below the cut off frequency.

explanation_steps: For light of a given frequency, intensity = (number of photons per unit area per unit time) × hf, so it is proportional to the photon flux (G12 pp.102, 104–112).
KEmax depends on frequency, not intensity (A false); the photocurrent is proportional to intensity (C false); emission needs f ABOVE the threshold (E false). Answer: B.

questions.stem: A point source of sound emits sound waves uniformly in all directions. The intensity of sound at a distance of 50 cm from the source is 3.6 × 10⁻⁸ W/m². The intensity level of the sound at a distance 300 cm from the source is (take the intensity I₀ = 1.0 × 10⁻¹² W/m²)
explanation_steps: Intensity from a point source falls as 1/r²: I₂ = I₁ (r₁/r₂)² = 3.6 × 10⁻⁸ × (50/300)² = 3.6 × 10⁻⁸ / 36 = 1.0 × 10⁻⁹ W/m².
Intensity level β = 10 log(I/I₀) = 10 log(10⁻⁹/10⁻¹²) = 10 × 3 = 30 dB (G11 pp.201–205). Answer: B.

questions.stem: A 500 kg of water is mixed with 5140 kg of unknown liquid. Assuming no change in volume, the average relative density of the mixture is 1.025. The density (in kg/m³) of the unknown liquid is
explanation_steps: Volume of water = 500 kg / 1000 kg/m³ = 0.500 m³. Total mass = 5640 kg; total volume = 5640/1025 = 5.502 m³ (G12 pp.4–10).
Volume of liquid = 5.502 − 0.500 = 5.002 m³; density = 5140/5.002 ≈ 1027 kg/m³ (relative density ≈ 1.03).

No option matches, and none can: a mixture denser than water (1.025) cannot contain only water and a liquid lighter than water, while all options are below 1 (and are written as relative densities although the stem asks for kg/m³). The item is faulty; C is keyed only nominally and every option is accepted.
tips: Mixture density = total mass / total volume – it always lies between the two densities.

similar_questions.stem: 200 kg of water is mixed with 300 kg of a liquid of relative density 1.5 (no volume change). What is the relative density of the mixture?
explanation_steps: Volumes: 0.200 m³ + 300/1500 = 0.200 m³ → total 0.400 m³; density = 500/0.400 = 1250 kg/m³ → relative density 1.25.

questions.review_flag: Faulty item: with the printed data the liquid's density is ≈ 1027 kg/m³; all options are < 1 (and in the wrong unit), which is impossible for a mixture of relative density 1.025. Nominal key C, all options accepted; teacher should void or correct the item.

questions.stem: Which of the following lights has a photon of greatest momentum?
explanation_steps: Photon momentum p = h/λ (= E/c = hf/c), so the shortest wavelength (highest frequency) has the greatest momentum (G12 pp.101–102).
Of the listed colours, blue has the shortest wavelength (≈ 450 nm; red ≈ 700 nm). Answer: B.

explanation_steps: E = hf; violet has the highest frequency of these. Answer: D.
